facts.statement: Choconsaurus was an extinct genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur within the group Titanosauriformes.
facts.quote: Choconsaurus ("El Chocón lizard") is an extinct genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur belonging to the group Titanosauriformes

facts.statement: Choconsaurus lived in what is now Argentina during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: which lived in the area of present-day Argentina during the Early Cretaceous

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Choconsaurus was discovered in Villa El Chocón, Neuquén province, Argentina, by Viviana Moro prior to 1996.
facts.quote: The holotype (specimen MMCh-PV 44/10) was found in Villa El Chocón in Neuquén province, Argentina by Viviana Moro before 1996

facts.statement: The species Choconsaurus baileywillisi was named and described in 2017 by Edith Simón, Leonardo Salgado, and Jorge Orlando Calvo.
facts.quote: In 2017, the species type Choconsaurus baileywillisi was named and described by Edith Simón, Leonardo Salgado and Jorge Orlando Calvo

facts.statement: The genus name Choconsaurus refers to the location of its discovery, El Chocón.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to its discovery in El Chocón

facts.statement: The species name baileywillisi honors American geologist Bailey Willis, who mapped the area's stratigraphy between 1910 and 1914.
facts.quote: the name of the species is in homage to the American geologist Bailey Willis, who traced the stratigraphy of the area between 1910 and 1914

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Choconsaurus was found in the Huincul Formation, dating to the Albian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was found in a layer of the Huincul Formation dating to the Albian stage

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull

facts.statement: The preserved remains include vertebrae from the neck, back, and tail, along with parts of the limbs.
facts.quote: The vertebrae of the neck, back and tail and parts of the limbs were preserved

facts.statement: Researchers identified that the upper edge of the posterior joint face on the cervical vertebrae was hardly developed.
facts.quote: In the cervical vertebrae, the upper edge of the face of the posterior joint was hardly developed

facts.statement: Choconsaurus lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 95 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica

facts.statement: The time range for Choconsaurus is estimated from 110.1 to 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Choconsaurus belongs to the class Sauropoda.
Choconsaurus is classified under the unranked family Titanosauria.
